items.label: Industry: Humanoid Robotics & Industrial Automation
items.detail: Selected via a live-searched news-prevalent theme: the IBKR connector was authenticated this session and current holdings (CCJ, CRWV, DBC, FCX, GOOG, IGLN, KGC, LLY, MPC, NEM, REMX, SSLV, TLT, TTWO, ULTA) were checked, but every one of those names already anchored a dedicated Scout cycle in the last seven weeks, so this run went with the clearest unscouted news-prevalent theme instead. 2026 has brought mega-round private financings (Apptronik's $520M extension at a ~$5B valuation backed by Google and Mercedes-Benz; Figure AI reportedly near a $39B valuation), the first clean path to a US-listed pure play (Agility Robotics' SPAC merger with Churchill Capital Corp XI, ticker to become AGLT, S-4 effective Oct 13 2026, shareholder vote Nov 2 2026), and a fresh US regulatory tailwind (FCC move in July 2026 to bar foreign-made advanced robotic devices, plus reported ~25% tariffs on Chinese robots) running against China's own push to formalize 100+ national humanoid-robot standards by 2028. Not covered by any prior scout cycle (critical minerals/precious metals 2026-08-31, GLP-1 2026-08-31, gaming 2026-09-06, search/ads/cloud 2026-09-13, nuclear/SMR 2026-09-20, neoclouds 2026-09-27, beauty & personal care retail 2026-10-04, US oil refining 2026-10-11).

items.label: NVDA
items.detail: NVIDIA -- not held (a same-day round-trip buy/sell on 2026-09-29/30 nets to no current position). The picks-and-shovels enabler of the whole theme via the Isaac robotics platform, Jetson Thor edge-compute module, and Project GR00T foundation models that underpin training/inference for most named humanoid programs; real risk is that humanoid robotics is an undisclosed, likely small slice of NVIDIA's total AI-compute revenue, so this is really a diversified AI-infrastructure position wearing a robotics label rather than concentrated humanoid exposure. Last $213.75 (IBKR snapshot, 2026-10-18).
items.diversification_note: The account currently has no direct AI-compute exposure after exiting its CRWV/GEV-adjacent neocloud positions this quarter; NVDA would reintroduce that exposure through the most diversified single name available rather than concentrating in one GPU-cloud operator.
items.suggested_size: Starter position; size as a broad AI-infrastructure add that happens to lead robotics compute, not as a concentrated robotics bet.

items.label: CCXI
items.detail: Churchill Capital Corp XI -- the SPAC merging with Agility Robotics (post-merger ticker AGLT) -- not held. The first direct, liquid, US-listed humanoid-robotics pure play with a near-term catalyst: S-4 declared effective Oct 13 2026, shareholder vote Nov 2 2026, close expected November 2026. Agility's Digit humanoid is already deployed commercially (seven units at Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada) with over $300M in committed Digit 5 orders, and the PIPE is anchored by Foxconn, a genuine manufacturing-scale strategic. Real risk: this is a pre-merger SPAC trading on deal-completion expectations rather than operating fundamentals -- redemption/vote risk remains live until Nov 2, and over 90% of recent de-SPACs have traded below their $10 reference price post-merger. Last $10.64 (IBKR snapshot, 2026-10-18), already above the ~$10 trust value.
items.diversification_note: No overlap with any current account holding; standalone new thematic exposure rather than a hedge or complement to an existing position.
items.suggested_size: Small speculative starter only, sized for binary deal-completion risk ahead of the Nov 2 vote; revisit sizing once the merger closes and AGLT reports as an operating company.

items.label: TER
items.detail: Teradyne -- not held. Owns Universal Robots (collaborative arms) and MiR (autonomous mobile robots), giving real, already-profitable revenue in adjacent industrial automation while the core semiconductor-test business cushions downside the pure humanoid names don't have; robotics segment revenue grew from $91M (Q1 2026) to $100M (Q2 2026), its fourth straight quarter of growth. Real risk: robotics is still only ~8% of total company revenue, so TER is primarily a semiconductor-test stock with a robotics kicker, and one unverified Robot Report teaser flagged a possible layoff round tied to the segment missing expectations, worth re-checking next earnings call. Last $323.60 (IBKR snapshot, 2026-10-18).
items.diversification_note: Adds semiconductor-test-cycle exposure the account does not currently have, alongside a small, already-revenue-generating slice of industrial robotics -- a lower-beta way into the theme than NVDA or CCXI.
items.suggested_size: Starter position; treat as core semiconductor-test exposure with a robotics optionality kicker, not the primary way to express the humanoid thesis.

items.label: SYM
items.detail: Symbotic -- not held. Warehouse-automation robotics (not humanoid, but the same 'replace repetitive physical labor with autonomous robots' thesis) with real commercial deployments and revenue today -- exactly the adoption-gap opportunity of fixed-footprint automation running ahead of general-purpose humanoids. Not yet a specific call: revenue is heavily weighted toward a small number of large retail/logistics customers, and valuation needs a closer look before sizing. Last $38.67 (IBKR snapshot, 2026-10-18).

items.label: RR
items.detail: Richtech Robotics -- not held. The most direct US-listed 'pure play' humanoid/service-robotics name available today ahead of AGLT's close, but at micro-cap scale with only ~$1.5M in Q2 FY2026 revenue -- genuine execution and penny-stock liquidity risk. Worth tracking as a speculative name to revisit if revenue scales meaningfully, not a call today. Last $1.29 (IBKR snapshot, 2026-10-18).

items.label: Humanoid robotics forecasting uncertainty and policy reversibility
items.detail: No specific ticker -- two risks sitting under every name in this report. First, credible market-size estimates span roughly $425M to $154B depending on year and scope, and even Goldman Sachs has revised its own 2035 base case upward multiple times, while private-market valuations (Figure at a reported $39B, Apptronik at ~$5B) are being set years ahead of proven unit economics -- a financing slowdown or a high-profile platform failure could reprice the whole theme quickly. Second, the current US tariff/FCC tailwind favoring domestic and allied suppliers over Chinese ones (UBTech, Unitree) is a 2026 policy choice, not a structural moat like a permitting barrier, and a negotiated tariff rollback or FCC rule reversal would remove the competitive edge this report leans on for NVDA/TER/AGLT. Worth revisiting both each cycle rather than treating either as settled.
